punchline: Ada Lovelace's notes ran three times longer than the article she translated, and in them she wrote that the engine can only do what we order it to do.
thirty_sec: In 1842 Luigi Menabrea wrote a French article on Babbage's Analytical Engine. Ada Lovelace translated it, then added seven notes, about three times as long, signed A. A. L. Note G laid out how the engine could compute Bernoulli numbers with a chain of operation cards. In the same note she wrote that the machine has no pretensions to originate anything; it does whatever we know how to order it to perform.
